assertion.rationale: F5 was already CLOSED (Task 3, see 3.12.3) before this control's F11 update: the dead node --check glob step in lint-ci.yml was deleted rather than patched, restoring npm test across all 7 workspaces to the required-checks gate. F11 is CLOSED (Task 14): Action.OpenUrl.url and Image.url in AdaptiveCardView.tsx are constrained by an /^https?:\/\//i allowlist (rejects javascript:, case-varied and whitespace-padded variants, data:, vbscript:; the fallback UnsupportedElement renders instead of a dropped/blank element), both nginx templates now emit a Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', required because Fluent UI v9's Griffel injects CSS-in-JS with no nonce wired up; connect-src scoped to Direct Line's REST+websocket host, the directline-token Function's default hostname, and the Application Insights Web SDK's config/ingestion hosts — verified in a real browser against the built bundle) plus X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy, and both frontend Dockerfiles now drop to USER nginx. F12 is now CLOSED (Task 15): scrubSql (apps/mcp-tools/src/tools/sql-dialect.ts) returns { text, terminated } instead of a bare string, and assertReadOnlySingleStatement rejects with an 'unterminated comment or quoted section' message BEFORE the single-statement check, the forbidden-verb check or the SELECT/WITH check run — so a partially-scrubbed scan result is never trusted by anything downstream. Block-comment nesting is now dialect-aware: depth is tracked only when dialect === 'tsql' (T-SQL genuinely nests, so a crafted `/* a /* b */` with one real close must stay open); for 'sqlite' the first `*/` closes, matching the real engine, which does not nest. Verified against the exact reproduction in F12: `SELECT 1 /* a /* b */ ; DELETE FROM launches` against 'tsql' now throws 'unterminated' (the comment genuinely never closes under T-SQL rules); the same text against 'sqlite' is correctly seen as a CLOSED comment (first */ wins) that exposes ' ; DELETE FROM launches' as a live second statement, which the pre-existing single-statement check now catches because it is no longer hidden by over-scrubbing; an unterminated backtick, quote or bracket is rejected the same way in both dialects. A legitimate non-nesting comment (`/* note: a/b ratio */`) still passes in both dialects, and all 27 pre-existing bypass probes (stacked statements, schema columns containing keyword substrings, string-literal contents, comment-smuggled verbs, WAITFOR, sp_/xp_ prefixes, SQLite file/schema escapes) still behave correctly — apps/mcp-tools test count moved from 277 to 287 (root suite: 858 -> 868, exit 0). This control has no other open contributor: F5, F11 and F12 — the only three findings in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md that cite 3.14.1 — are all CLOSED.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. (Deleting lint-ci's dead node-test step, Task 3/3.12.3; the Adaptive Card URL allowlist, CSP and non-root nginx user, Task 14; and the dialect-aware structural-validity check in the SQL gate, Task 15, are all DONE.) A regression here — the lint-ci node leg reintroduced and silently broken again, an unguarded Action/element url or a CSP relaxation, or scrubSql's nesting reverted to dialect-blind — would reopen this control.
